title: terraform-kms-hsm-secretstore-connector-module
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a reusable Terraform module that standardizes KMS/HSM integration and secrets management for Private (VPC) deployments. The module must support common cloud and customer-managed options: AWS KMS + AWS Secrets Manager, AWS CloudHSM for BYOH use-cases, Azure Key Vault HSM, and an opinionated HashiCorp Vault integration (transit auto-unseal and secret engines). The goal is to provide a single, composable module teams can plug into Private deployment stacks to: provision keys, configure access policies/grants, wire secrets backends (Secrets Manager or Vault), and deploy lightweight health checks and rotation hooks. The module should include upgrade safety patterns (key rotation handling, state migrations, rolling secret re-reads) and clear operational runbooks. This ticket covers design, initial implementation, tests, and a first integration example used by the private control-plane helm charts.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module publishes as /modules/kms-hsm-secretstore with semver tagging and clear inputs/outputs
Supports at least: AWS KMS (+grant creation), AWS CloudHSM (BYOH mapping), and HashiCorp Vault transit auto-unseal configuration
Provides an option to wire secrets to AWS Secrets Manager or Vault KV v2 with example usage for EC2, ECS, and Kubernetes workloads
Includes automated health checks (Terraform-managed CloudWatch synthetic lambda or k8s probe manifest) and a documented failure mode checklist
Has Terratest/integration tests that run in CI against an ephemeral account or localstack where applicable
Security review completed and acceptance sign-off from Security and SRE
Migration guide documented for customers with existing KMS keys or Vault backends (no secret plaintext in state)
implementation_notes: Module layout: submodules per provider (aws, azure, vault) with a thin root module that exposes unified inputs
Use provider-agnostic naming for outputs (e.g., key_id, key_arn, vault_transit_path) to simplify platform wiring
Avoid storing secret plaintext in Terraform state: prefer writing secret metadata and using providers' secret objects or Vault transit encryption for import flows
For AWS KMS: create customer-managed key when requested, create minimal key policy + iam roles/grants for Redwood service principals, and provide alias and rotation schedule toggle
For CloudHSM: provide guidance and resource placeholders; where tight integration is impossible in Terraform (customer-managed HSM appliances), expose inputs and example runbook for manual mapping
For Vault: support both managed Vault (customer-provided) and our recommended self-managed Vault via Helm. Implement transit auto-unseal examples and a Vault role + policy generator in the module

Health checks: implement a small lambda that performs a quick encrypt/decrypt against KMS or transit encrypt/decrypt to assert key availability and proper IAM; deploy as CloudWatch synthetic alarm or k8s LivenessProbe for private control-plane
Upgrade safety: design key rotation to create new keys and rotate aliases rather than reusing keys; document steps and provide terraform plan examples for safe rotation

Testing: Terratest cases for create/destroy, encryption/decryption roundtrip, IAM restrictions, and module input permutations; use mock Vault for unit tests and real ephemeral resources for CI smoke tests
rollout_plan: Week 1 (design + API): finalize module inputs/outputs and publish design doc to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/KMS+HSM+Secretstore+Module
Week 2 (implementation): implement AWS KMS + Secrets Manager flow and Vault transit samples; open GH draft PR under infra/modules#42
Week 3 (tests + security): add Terratest suites, run internal CI smoke-runs, and address Security review findings
Week 4 (integration): integrate with private control-plane helm chart as an example and run E2E in staging; prepare migration doc
Canary: enable module for a single customer/staging cluster before wide release and monitor healthchecks for 72 hours
test_plan: Unit: validate input var schema and output formatting with terraform validate and fmt
Integration: Terratest create/destroy, encrypt/decrypt roundtrip using KMS and Vault transit
CI smoke: run module against ephemeral AWS account with minimal permissions and report resources created
Security tests: ensure secrets never appear in state or logs; run automated scanning for IAM overprivilege
Chaos test: simulate KMS key unavailable and assert healthcheck alarms fire and documented fallback behavior triggers
